articles.title: Jayden Daniels to visit with specialists after sustaining dislocated elbow in loss to Cowboys
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels is once again battling a dislocated elbow.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders find themselves in a familiar — and unfortunate — situation after star quarterback Jayden Daniels left Sunday's game with a dislocated left elbow. After undergoing further testing Monday, Daniels will meet with specialists to consult on the injury, Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Monday.

Quinn added the team won't have a major update on Daniels until those meetings happen. For now, however, the Commanders are not looking to bring in another quarterback.

Daniels sustained the injury on the final play of the first half in a 37-20 loss to the Dallas Cowboys . With the Commanders looking to score before halftime, Daniels took a snap from under center, but awkwardly tripped after one of his linemen appeared to step on his foot, knocking him off-balance. As he was going to the ground, Daniels used his left arm to brace himself.

After chucking the ball incomplete, Daniels lay on the turf until he was eventually carted off the field.

It was a gruesome injury, one that caused Tom Brady — who was in the broadcast booth — to utter an expletive live on the air . Brady quickly apologized for swearing.

After the contest, the Commanders head coach revealed Daniels was dealing with a dislocated left elbow. Quinn added that X-rays did not show a fracture, but that Daniels would undergo additional testing Monday.

It's an injury that Daniels has dealt with before. The 25-year-old missed four games last season due to a dislocated left elbow . He returned to action, but reinjured himself in his first game back and was shut down for the rest of the year. Quinn said Monday that surgery was not mentioned last season, with a source telling ESPN that Daniels did not sustain ligament damage last year, which is why surgery was not recommended at the time.

That injury completely derailed what was supposed to be a star-studded second season for the quarterback. As a rookie, Daniels looked like a future superstar. After being selected No. 2 overall from LSU by the Commanders, Daniels threw 25 touchdowns against nine interceptions as a rookie, leading Washington to the playoffs and making the Pro Bowl in his first year.

His numbers took a massive downturn in Year 2 due to various injuries. Daniels started just seven games last season, tossing eight touchdowns against three interceptions.

With those injuries seemingly behind him, Daniels opened the 2026 NFL season looking to get back on track. After a slow start in Week 1 against the Philadelphia Eagles , Daniels rallied late to nearly lead his team to a win.

The quarterback was off to a modest start against the Cowboys before leaving the contest at the end of the first half.

With Daniels once again sidelined, the Commanders will turn to veteran Marcus Mariota in Week 3. The 32-year-old Mariota performed admirably when pressed into action last season, but went just 2-6 in his eight starts.

articles.title: ‘He Should Not Be Starting,’ ‘What Are We Doing?’ — Buccaneers Fans React to HC Todd Bowles Contradicting Rueben Bain Jr. Over Injury Status
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have gotten off to a surprisingly poor start this season. After losing to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 1, they fell to the Clevela...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have gotten off to a surprisingly poor start this season. After losing to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 1, they fell to the Cleveland Browns in their home opener in a dreadful performance. Now the Buccaneers sit 0-2, and plenty of panic is spreading among the fanbase.

The Buccaneers need to be better on both sides of the ball, but a few specific players have been called out for low production. One is rookie defensive end Rueben Bain Jr. While it usually takes rookies some time to get acclimated to the NFL, the team needs something from their first-round pick given how much they are struggling on defense.

Buccaneers Fans Critical of Rueben Bain Jr.'s Situation

Bain looked dominant during training camp, and that raised the level of expectation for the rookie in his first season. However, we have not seen the same player in the first two weeks. Bain insists he is not injured, but Bucs head coach Todd Bowles is not convinced.

JoeBucsFan.com reported that "Bain says the shoulder is not affecting his play, per Bowles. However, it sounded like Bowles is skeptical."

"I don't think he's completely healthy," Bowles said of Bain. "But at the same time, he's good enough to play. We've got to get more production there."

For Latest Information: NFL Injury Report

Bowles' comments seem to contradict what the rookie believes about his health, and the team's fans were quick to react to it.

Joshua A. Martin said on X, "If Bain is not healthy, sit him down! He deserves to be out on the field healthy. He clearly isn't the same player as we seen during the preseason/training camp."

One fan wrote, "Then he should not be starting," in reference to Bowles saying Bain isn't fully healthy.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Another fan added, "Currently looks like Walker is better at this point if Bain isn't healthy – WTF we doing here?!"

The Walker referenced is David Walker , the Bucs' fourth-round pick last season. In limited snaps, he recorded a sack against the Browns, and that is more than you can say for Bain.

Evan T on X had a similar response to Bain playing many more snaps than Walker. He said, "David Walker played like what — 3 snaps and had a sack? What are we doing???????"

It seems like Buccaneers fans are fed up with the defensive rotations to begin the season. Most of that is directed at Bowles, a defense-minded head coach who has the final say on who is on the field.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Through two games, the Bucs are giving up 28 points per game, and their defense is ranked 15th on PFN's Defense Impact Metric . That won't cut it, especially for a team whose offense has struggled so far.

The Bucs have plenty of time to turn their season around, but they need more on both sides of the ball. Developing Bain and other rookies will also go a long way toward their being successful.

Naresh said on X, "My big worry is he is not gonna get properly developed because of this Coaching Staff."

Bowles may find himself on the hot seat if he does not turn things around fast. Buccaneers fans aren't used to being uncompetitive, and that is the path they are currently on.

articles.title: The best of the (actually funny) Caleb Williams injury memes
articles.summary: There were some pretty vicious Caleb Williams memes, but others were downright funny. Perhaps even to Caleb himself.
articles.body:
The good news for Bears QB Caleb Williams is that his injured hamstring is about as good as he or the team could have hoped.

The bad news? Social media is roasting Williams' real-time reaction to the injury when it happened. Some are funny. Others are downright vicious, questioning the toughness of the same quarterback who got beat to a pulp as a rookie.

If you watched Williams go down late in Sunday's game, it was a pretty shocking moment. He fell untouched and writhed in pain, unable to get up immediately. Solder Field, already a bit down after a bad offensive day and three hours in the rain, fell silent.

Now that we know Williams' hamstring didn't detach from the bone, it was open season. You knew it was bound to happen.

The Keyboard Corps is really leaning into the same through line on most of these: that being carted off for a short-term injury is a serious affront. Even former NFL players got in on the action.

But we're going to veer away from that type of response. Some of the Williams memes were downright funny. These were jokes that maybe even Williams could possibly laugh at. You know, when he's feeling better. (Watch it!)

It felt like this one was made specifically for my wife.

Anyone who has kids knows this one is good.

I'd rather step on a jellyfish than a Lego piece. Seriously. They're colored caltrops for kids.

Lieutenant Dan had more than a grade-1 hammy.

There actually were multiple "Forrest Gump"-related memes, including this well-worn trope.

This is absurd, but mesmerizingly funny, too.

This one has a whole series, including burning your mouth on a Hot Pocket …

This is just good, clean fun from where I'm sitting.

Williams is going to be asked about this — or these memes — at some point. Maybe it's not this week, as head coach Ben Johnson said Williams might not practice. But eventually, Williams will be asked.

I'll be curious about his reaction to them. There are some parallels to the Paul Pierce situation from a generation ago. In Game 1 of the 2008 NBA Finals, Pierce had to be carried off the floor, yet he miraculously returned in just a few game minutes to make a few buckets and go on to win Finals MVP.

The backstory of that one isn't clear. Did Pierce really use the "injury" as an excuse to use the commode? Maybe, even if Pierce's story has wavered on that one over the years.

If Williams has fun with it, it could turn in his favor. If not? It might be the kind of thing fans hang around his neck for every tough game, every tough playoff loss or — yep — every time he gets hurt in a game.

We'd hate to see that. And you can probably tell, these memes are mostly in the we-all-can-laugh-without-being-mean category. Some are downright terrific.

The rest? Most of us have already moved on from those.
